## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

23	// The endpoint is a ROUTINE'S API TRIGGER — `POST /v1/claude_code/routines/
24	// <trigger-id>/fire` with a per-routine bearer token — which is what Claude Code
25	// on the web actually exposes to an HTTP caller. Three consequences the design's
26	// "a CCR API call" did not spell out, each verified against the routines docs
27	// rather than assumed:
28	//
29	//  - THE BEHAVIOR IS THE ROUTINE'S STORED PROMPT, not ours. `text` reaches the
30	//    session wrapped in a `<routine-fire-payload>` block explicitly labelled
31	//    untrusted, and a routine acts on it only because its own saved prompt says
32	//    to. That is the issue-is-data posture arriving for free at one more hop: our
33	//    payload names an item, and every instruction comes from a stored artifact.
34	//    The routine's stored prompt is one line pointing at `instructions.md` beside
35	//    this file, so the whole of what a session does is tracked and reviewed.
36	//  - THE BODY CARRIES ONE FIELD. `text` is freeform and unparsed — structured
37	//    JSON would arrive as a literal string — so the item number and nonce go in
38	//    as prose, and nothing else goes in at all.
39	//  - THERE IS NO IDEMPOTENCY KEY (standing entry 11, answered: the endpoint
40	//    offers none), which is exactly why THIS MODULE CALLS ONCE PER ITEM AND NEVER
41	//    RETRIES. A retry is only safe when you know the first call did nothing, and
42	//    a client-side timeout is the one case where you cannot know — the session
43	//    may well have started. Retrying there is what would make invocation
44	//    at-least-once and put two sessions on one item; declining to retry is what
45	//    keeps it at-most-once and lets the whole agent-side claim protocol delete.
46	//    An outcome we did not learn is reported as UNKNOWN and resolved by the agent
47	//    leash, which is a rule that already exists, rather than by a guess here.
48	//
49	// The beta header is dated and the endpoint is a research preview whose two most
50	// recent header versions keep working, so it lives in config with a default here
51	// — a rotation is then a config edit on one repo, never an engine release the
52	// whole fleet waits for.
53	export const DEFAULT_HEADERS = Object.freeze({
54	  'anthropic-beta': 'experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01',
55	  'anthropic-version': '2023-06-01',
56	});
57	
58	// The endpoint a task's hand-off calls, resolved against the repo's config.
59	// Returns `{ name, url, tokenEnv, headers }` or `{ name, error }` — a task naming
60	// an endpoint the repo has not configured is a repo-configuration fact, reported
61	// where the operator reads it, never a crash.
62	export function resolveEndpoint(config, task) {
63	  const name = task?.decl?.invocation_endpoint ?? DEFAULT_ENDPOINT;
64	  const endpoints = config?.taskScheduler?.endpoints ?? {};
65	  const entry = endpoints[name];
66	  if (!entry) {
67	    return { name, error: `this repo's config declares no invocation endpoint "${name}" (taskScheduler.endpoints)` };
68	  }
69	  if (!entry.url) return { name, error: `invocation endpoint "${name}" declares no url` };
70	  if (!entry.tokenSecret) return { name, error: `invocation endpoint "${name}" declares no tokenSecret (the NAME of the repo Actions secret holding its token)` };
71	  return { name, url: entry.url, tokenEnv: entry.tokenSecret, headers: { ...DEFAULT_HEADERS, ...(entry.headers ?? {}) } };
72	}
73	
74	// The fire payload: which item, and the nonce that proves this call is the one
75	// the hand-off comment recorded. Prose, not JSON — the field is freeform and
76	// unparsed, so a structured payload would arrive as a literal string — and
77	// deliberately free of instructions, because the routine's stored prompt is what
78	// says how to act on it (see `instructions.md`). The session still validates
79	// the item in code before touching it: a payload labelled untrusted is trusted no
80	// more than a label event was.
81	export const firePayload = ({ repo, item, nonce }) =>
82	  `Claudinite work item: ${repo}#${item.number}. Invocation nonce: ${nonce}.`;
83	
84	// The invoker seam the executor calls, exactly once per item. Failure is DATA,
85	// never a throw, and it comes in two kinds the caller must treat differently:
86	//
87	//   { ok: true, sessionId, sessionUrl }   the routine fired; a session exists
88	//   { ok: false, answered: true, error }  the endpoint ANSWERED and refused —
89	//                                         no session, and the cause is a
90	//                                         configuration fault a retry cannot fix
91	//   { ok: false, answered: false, error } no answer reached us — a timeout, a
92	//                                         dropped connection. The session may or
93	//                                         may not exist, and nothing here may
94	//                                         guess which.
95	export function agentInvoker({ repo, config, env = process.env, fetchImpl = fetch, timeoutMs = 60e3 }) {
96	  return async function invoke({ task, item, nonce }) {
97	    const endpoint = resolveEndpoint(config, task);
98	    // A configuration fault, decided before any call: definite, and no session.
99	    if (endpoint.error) return { ok: false, answered: true, error: endpoint.error };
100	    const token = env[endpoint.tokenEnv];
101	    if (!token) {
102	      // The `required_secrets` posture, applied to the endpoint token: nothing
103	      // fails silently, the task just doesn't work yet, and the item names which
104	      // secret to set (DESIGN §14.7).
105	      return { ok: false, answered: true, error: `the Actions secret \`${endpoint.tokenEnv}\` for invocation endpoint "${endpoint.name}" is not set in this repo` };
106	    }
107	
108	    const payload = { text: firePayload({ repo, item, nonce }) };
109	
110	    // ONE call. No loop, and deliberately no `attempts` knob for anyone to raise.
111	    try {
112	      const res = await fetchImpl(endpoint.url, {
113	        method: 'POST',
114	        headers: {
115	          ...endpoint.headers,
116	          'content-type': 'application/json',
117	          authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
118	          'user-agent': 'claudinite-executor',
119	        },
120	        body: JSON.stringify(payload),
121	        signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs),
122	      });
123	      let json = null;
124	      try { json = await res.json(); } catch { json = null; }
125	      if (res.status >= 200 && res.status < 300) {
126	        return {
127	          ok: true,
128	          sessionId: json?.claude_code_session_id ?? null,
129	          sessionUrl: json?.claude_code_session_url ?? null,
130	        };
131	      }
132	      // A status came back, so the endpoint decided: no session was started, and
133	      // the cause is a token, a URL or a routine — none of which a retry fixes.
134	      return {
135	        ok: false, answered: true,
136	        error: `endpoint "${endpoint.name}" returned ${res.status}${json?.error ? `: ${JSON.stringify(json.error)}` : ''}`,
137	      };
138	    } catch (e) {
139	      // Nothing came back. The request may have landed and started a session, so
140	      // this is the one outcome that must never be retried and never be reported
141	      // as a failure — it is genuinely unknown, and the caller says so on the item.
142	      return { ok: false, answered: false, error: `endpoint "${endpoint.name}" gave no answer: ${e.message}` };
143	    }
144	  };

# Working in the canary

This repo is Claudinite's **live canary**. Read this before changing anything here, because the
normal instinct — make the repo green, make the repo useful — is wrong in a specific way.

## The gate this repo is half of

Canon CI can prove a canon change is internally consistent. It cannot prove the change is safe for
**consumers**: the vendored mount, the pack loader, the hook wiring and the skill mounts only meet
a real repo on the other side of a vendor set. So the canon runs
`.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml`, which converges *this* repo against a candidate canon ref
and runs the world sweep and the selftest against the result.

The gate's whole value rests on this repo being a **real, disposable member**. Real, or the
rehearsal tests a shape no consumer has. Disposable, or nobody will let the rehearsal converge it.

## What must not be removed

Anything that makes this a member is load-bearing:

- the vendored mount at `.claudinite/shared/` and the `.claudinite-checks.json` declaration
  that names what is vendored;
- the `.claude/settings.json` hook registrations;
- the vendored scheduler workflow, with the repo-hashed cron minute;
- the unfiltered conformance workflow;
- **the `local/canary` pack** — the highest-value shape here. Canon #555 broke the fleet through
  exactly this surface: a local pack's manifest, its rules in both scopes, its bundled skills.

## Reading a red rehearsal

A rehearsal failure is a claim about the **candidate canon ref**, not about this repo. Before
touching anything here, separate the two:

1. **Does the same failure reproduce against canon `main`?** If it does, the canary drifted or
   broke on its own and the candidate ref is exonerated. Re-baseline to `main` and re-run.
2. **Only the candidate ref fails?** That is the signal the gate exists to produce. Fix it in the
   canon. Do not fix it here — a canary patched to stay green is a canary that has stopped
   reporting.
3. **Never quiet a finding with an `accept` entry to get a rehearsal green.** An `accept` is a
   reasoned keep about *this repo's* content; using one to mask a canon regression converts a
   loud failure into a silent one, permanently.

## Repairing the canary

Re-baselining to canon `main` is always the correct repair, and there is no local state here worth
preserving. One caveat, from vendoring's anti-rewind guard (#328): the stamped `ref` in
`.claudinite-checks.json` must be an **ancestor of canon `main`**. Stamp a feature-branch sha and
the repo lands `ref-not-on-trunk`, which convergence then refuses to rewind past — wedging the
repo permanently. Rehearsals may stamp a candidate ref by design; a human repair should not.

1	# Growth — dedup local packs against the canon (per repo)
2	
3	The growth lifecycle's pruning stage: reconcile this repo's **local packs** against the shared **canon** it
4	consumes (Claudinite, vendored read-only), pruning local items — a pack's prose line, or a whole local check —
5	the canon now covers. It lands the run's prunes through a single PR against the repo's default branch,
6	**delivered to land** per the repo's own delivery settings. Often there's nothing to prune, and that's fine. You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue, whose
7	**Context** is **binding scope — not a hint** (the executor will not let you re-decide or widen it).
8	
9	> This task only prunes local packs against the canon; lifting local items up into the canon is the central
10	> promote task's job (canon-side).
11	
12	## Conventions used in this doc
13	
14	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
15	- **GitHub access is MCP-native.** Updating the tracking issue and opening the PR go through the session's
16	  **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub access — the shell reaches
17	  only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so never reach for `gh`/`curl` or
18	  a cross-repo clone.
19	- **The mounted canon.** The exact canon revision this repo currently consumes — compare against *that*, not a
20	  live fetch. It is what `.claudinite/shared/` holds at the mount's stamp (a promotion is visible here only
21	  once baselining has converged the mount to include it). Prune only against what the repo actually mounts.
22	- **The dispatch's Context narrows the *yardstick*, never the local surface.** When the Context names
23	  newly-changed canon packs ("Re-check local items against these newly-changed canon packs: …"), **those packs
24	  are this run's entire yardstick**: every prune must cite a line or rule id from one of *them*, and you never
25	  widen the comparison to the rest of the mounted canon. What is *not* narrowed is the local side — **every**
26	  local item is in play against those packs, whatever it is about. (Local pack names are unrelated to canon
27	  pack names, so there is nothing to match up.) A dispatch with **no** Context block carries no such bound: the
28	  precondition emits the list only when the mounted canon moved, and its other arm — the repo's own local packs
29	  changed — deliberately emits none, so that run compares the fresh local items against the whole mounted canon.
30	- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) —
31	  everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the
32	  rename window). That's the corpus this task prunes within; the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under
33	  `.claudinite/` is never a prune target, only the yardstick you prune *against*.
34	
35	## The method lives in the skill
36	
37	What to prune, strip, or rephrase; the keep-test (an item that says *more* than the canon stays; one that
38	only says it in repo-specific names goes); how a canon **check** covers an item more strongly than prose;
39	and the shrink-only discipline — all of that is owned by the
40	[**growth-dedup** skill](../../skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md). Follow it; don't re-derive it here. This
41	worker only frames the unattended run around it.
42	
43	## Discipline
44	
45	- **Only remove a local item you can show the mounted canon genuinely covers — quote the canon line (or the
46	  covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson.
47	- **Open a single PR against `main`** from a per-run-unique branch (see
48	  [the git-github-advanced skill](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md)) — one PR for the
49	  whole run's prunes, not one per item — never a direct push. **Title the commit and the PR
50	  `Claudinite growth: dedup local packs`** — the `growth-write-scope` check keys on that title to certify the
51	  run pruned only the repo's local packs. Then **deliver it by the shared procedure —
52	  [deliver-pr.md](../../../../engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md)**. That procedure — never this file — owns every
53	  landing nuance: it reads this repo's `maintenance.delivery` (a `review` repo's PR waits for the owner — still
54	  a delivered outcome) and arms auto-merge where the repo allows it. Do not assume this run's PR merges
55	  unreviewed — that is the repo's setting, not this task's (the declared ceiling is `merged-pr`: it *may*
56	  land). What holds the prune bar on the default settings is the quote-the-canon-line discipline above, the
57	  `dedup-prune-integrity` and `growth-write-scope` checks, and CI — never a reviewer's second look, which a
58	  wrongful prune is easy to wave through anyway. **Put the issue reference in the commit message** —
59	  `Refs #<n>` for this task's tracking issue (below), in the commit itself, not only the PR body. The repo's
60	  `basics` `task-lifecycle` check gates a PR on its commits referencing an issue, so a prune commit that cites
61	  none reds the repo's CI and blocks the merge.
62	- If an edit touches something a test reads, run the repo's offline test suite and keep it green before pushing.
63	
64	## Tracking
65	
66	The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:
67	
68	> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Dedup**
69	
70	Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number**. A run that finds no issue under
71	the exact title just creates one (closed). **Never open, close, or reopen it** afterward — its state carries no
72	meaning, only the log does. Log each run that changed a doc as a **dated comment** — naming what was pruned and
73	the canon line that now covers it. A run that prunes nothing logs nothing.
74	
75	## Run on a capable model
76	
77	Proving the mounted canon genuinely covers a local item before pruning it — and telling "the canon now owns
78	this" from "the canon states this too generally, keep the local cut" — is a **judgment call**. A downgraded
79	model prunes a real lesson, and on the default delivery settings the PR carrying it lands once CI passes —
80	there is no reviewer downstream to catch what the run got wrong. This task declares `agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.
81	
82	## What this task must never do
83	
84	- **Never edit the read-only canon** — it only prunes the repo's *local packs* against it, and the
85	  `growth-write-scope` check reds a run that touches anything outside them.
86	- **Never land a prune outside a PR** — every prune rides the run's single PR, delivered by
87	  [deliver-pr.md](../../../../engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md); a direct push to `main` is never in scope, and
88	  neither is merging past a red check or a repo whose delivery setting says `review`.
89	- **Never prune a local item without quoting the mounted-canon line (or covering check rule id) that covers
90	  it** — when unsure, leave it.
91	- **Never widen the dispatch's Context.** If it named the changed canon packs, a prune citing coverage from
92	  any *other* canon pack is out of scope for this run — leave the item; the cycle that moves that pack will
93	  reach it.
94	- **Never prune a local item that makes a stronger point about a narrower case** than the canon — that isn't
95	  redundancy. (A local item that only restates the canon in repo-specific names *is* prunable once the canon
96	  covers the point.)
97	- **Never let a dedup edit grow an entry or re-import canon prose** — every action removes portable text;
98	  the skill owns the strip discipline, and the `dedup-prune-integrity` check (this pack) is the backstop
99	  that reds the session when a dedup-labeled commit grows a local-pack prose file or restates a canon rule.

7	// `.github/workflows/` is diverted to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, staged into the
8	// maintenance PR as an ordinary added file, and the update ends at `apply-stage` until a
9	// session with an MCP credential moves it into place (#649).

11	// That lane had one exercised caller: the scheduler workflow's own convergence. A
12	// RECORD'S `materialize` shares the same `write`, and had never run against a live
13	// member — which is the residual #649 reopened for. This pack is the thing that makes
14	// it runnable: an inert workflow, delivered to a real repo by the real lane, whose
15	// content the canon then changes so the delivery has to happen again.
16	//
17	// WHY A PACK AND NOT A FIXTURE. The lane's failure mode is precisely what a fixture
18	// cannot see — a token's refusal, on a real push, against a real repository. A hermetic
19	// rehearsal proves the staging directory got a file; only a member proves the file
20	// arrives in `.github/workflows/`. So the probe has to be adoptable content that a
21	// member really declares, and adoptable content in this corpus is a pack.

2	// (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §6). Prunes local-pack items the canon now
3	// covers, keeping items the canon states too generally; lands the prunes through
4	// one PR against the default branch, delivered per the repo's delivery settings.
5	// Worker: task.md.
6	//
7	// The old fleet's `relevantCanonChanged` becomes the `sharedMount` signal — a
8	// declared pack's vendored files moving is the local echo of "the canon this repo
9	// mounts changed" — so movement, never the calendar, is what wakes this: a quiet
10	// repo with no local packs skips.
11	//
12	// The cadence is WEEKLY, not daily (#582). A member's mount moves most nights —
13	// baselining converges it daily — so a daily slot fired this opus dispatch, and the
14	// PR behind it, nearly every night. Pruning is not latency-sensitive: a
15	// local item the canon has already absorbed stays harmlessly correct until it goes,
16	// so the daily slot bought noise rather than freshness. Nothing is missed by the
17	// move — both signals below are WINDOW-scoped, and the collection window is the
18	// widest due task's period, so the weekly run sees a full 7 days of canon and
19	// local-pack movement batched into one dispatch.
20	//
21	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
22	
23	export default {
24	  id: 'growth-dedup',
25	  frequency: 'weekly',             // the weekly anchor — prunes against the mounted canon that morning's 02:00 baselining converged (DESIGN §2)
26	  precondition_signals: ['localPacks', 'sharedMount', 'commits'],
27	  agent_model: 'opus',                   // proving the canon genuinely covers a local item — and telling coverage from "stated too generally" — is a judgment call
28	  expected_outcome: 'merged-pr',            // one PR per run, delivered to land per the repo's delivery settings (a `review` member degrades it to open-pr)
29	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
30	  agent_execution_timeout: 1800,            // proving canon coverage per local item — generous bound, extreme protection
31	
32	  // Gate: the repo must actually track local packs (no local packs → nothing to
33	  // prune, self-skip). Given local packs, run when the mounted canon this repo
34	  // CARES about moved — a declared pack's vendored files changed (`sharedMount`),
35	  // which can newly cover a local item — or the repo's own local packs changed in
36	  // the window (a fresh local item to re-check against the canon). A quiet repo
37	  // with local packs but no relevant movement skips.
38	  precondition(signals) {
39	    const local = signals.localPacks ?? {};
40	    // `present` is null when the scheduler couldn't determine it; treat only an
41	    // explicit false as "definitely no local packs to prune".
42	    if (local.present === false) {
43	      return { run: false, reason: 'no local packs — nothing to prune' };
44	    }
45	    const changedPacks = signals.sharedMount?.changedPacks ?? [];
46	    const canonMoved = changedPacks.length > 0;
47	    const localChanged = local.changedInWindow === true;
48	
49	    if (canonMoved) {
50	      return { run: true, reason: `declared pack(s) changed in the mounted canon: ${changedPacks.join(', ')} — local items may now be covered`, context: [`Re-check local items against these newly-changed canon packs: ${changedPacks.join(', ')}.`] };
51	    }
